name: OPERA
reason: arXiv 2608.05990 (v1, 2026-08-06, not withdrawn) matches: operator-residual framework for LLM-agent optical experiments across three tasks (beam shaping with SLM, structured-light 3D reconstruction, interferometry). Closure claim verified from the paper's own text: decision loops ran in digital twins; 'Protocols were frozen before transfer, and hardware residuals were not returned to the agent' - so the physical loop is NOT agent-closed (not A5); three physical instruments served as open-loop validation. Official MIT repo (github.com/ningxu1995/OPERA, first author Ning Xu) plus Zenodo archive 10.5281/zenodo.21504254 (MIT, published 2026-07-23), both matching the paper.

record.name: OPERA

paper_links.label: arXiv:2608.05990 - OPERA: Operator-residual feedback for reliable autonomous optical experiments with language-model agents

record.inputs: Optical experiment tasks in digital twins; library of optical operators (executable changes to measurement, control, reconstruction) and physically interpretable residuals
record.outputs: Selected/combined/generated operator protocols, residual-based evaluations against withheld references, frozen protocols executed on three physical optical instruments (SLM beam shaping, structured-light 3D reconstruction, interferometry)
record.notes: LLM agent closes an iterative operator-selection loop in digital twins using physics-grounded residuals instead of hackable scores (score-only feedback produced non-physical score gains in 23.6-39.0% of decisions vs 0.9-1.9% with residuals). Not a physical closed loop: protocols were frozen before transfer to the three optical instruments and hardware residuals were not returned to the agent, so physical execution is open-loop validation.
aliases: Operator-residual feedback for reliable autonomous optical experiments

record.name: CRAFTS

record.outputs: Typed intermediate artifacts (VisualGraphIR, TopologyIR, SpecIR, BuildPlan, SolveReport), executable solved IDAES/Pyomo process models, eligible optimization results
